beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The shared workplace gives these ideas a visible form in Chapter Two.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Explorer organizes projects and artifacts, while WebChat carries assignments and clarification.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: WebMeet explores collaboration where a Robot can participate within an explicit role.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A meeting decision can become a task that changes a shared artifact.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The interesting question is what happens when collaboration includes software that can act.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The text connects presence, attribution, permissions, and the continuity of project work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its interface discussion therefore reveals part of the argument, beyond screen design.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers interested in collaboration can follow that thread from conversation to accountable action.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The technical chapter explains what the proposed workplace would need underneath.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It covers executable capabilities, persistent homes, tool interfaces, and deployment choices.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A model still needs tools and an environment where those tools can operate.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A directory can preserve state without providing an adequate execution boundary.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These distinctions connect the visible experience to engineering responsibilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You can approach this chapter with practical questions already in mind.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: What must remain persistent, what can change, and what actually enforces the boundary?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The details then become reasons for design choices, rather than a catalog of infrastructure.
